sample.question:
Gear Train is a mechanical reasoning puzzle. Several spur gears are mounted on a fixed panel; gears never move sideways, they can only spin in place. Two gears are meshed if and only if their toothed rims touch in the image. Each gear is labeled with a letter and its number of teeth is printed under the letter (for example '12T' means 12 teeth). Meshed gears obey two laws: (1) they always spin in opposite directions, and (2) they pass the same number of teeth per unit time, so teeth_A x turns_A = teeth_B x turns_B. The driver gear is marked with a red circular arrow showing its spin direction. A chain of meshed gears forming a closed loop with an ODD number of gears cannot spin at all - the whole train jams.

Look at the panel and count: how many gears are directly meshed with gear G? Answer with a single number.
sample.analysis:
Checking the image, the toothed rim of gear G touches the rim(s) of: E, F.
All meshing pairs in the panel are: A-B, C-E, D-H, D-I, E-G, E-H, F-G.
Therefore gear G is directly meshed with 2 gear(s).
So the answer is 2.

state_content.rules: meshed gears spin in opposite directions; teeth x turns is equal for meshed gears; an odd loop jams
